ORCL.notes: Headline non-GAAP diluted EPS ($2.11) includes one-time investment gains from asset sales (Ampere/Bloom Energy); ex-item it is $2.03 per a footnote easy to miss. The release states no gross-margin percentage at all (cost is presented by segment - cloud/software/hardware/services - not COGS), and next-quarter (Q1 FY27) revenue guidance is given only as a YoY growth-rate range (27-29%) rather than a dollar figure, so guide_rev cannot be derived. Capex appears only as an annual FY total ($55.7B) or trailing-4-quarter sums, never as a single quarter, and full-year guidance is 'confirmed' (revenue) while EPS guidance is explicitly 'raise[d]' - a mixed signal resolved here as raised because that is the explicit verb used. Full-year FY27 revenue guide IS stated: 'we confirm our prior revenue guidance of $90 billion total revenue' - recorded as a point FY guide.

MU.notes: YoY revenue growth (+345.7%, AI/DRAM boom) is never stated as a percentage anywhere - only dollar comparisons to the prior quarter and year-ago quarter - so it must be computed from $41,456M vs $9,301M. The main cash-flow statement shows only 9-month cumulative capex ($19,602M); the true single-quarter figure ($7,826M gross / $7,084M 'net' of government-incentive proceeds) appears only in the separate free-cash-flow reconciliation table. Guidance is quarter-only (FQ4-26); there is no annual guidance in this release at all, so guide_raised is null rather than 'maintained'.

ADBE.notes: Adobe never states an actual GAAP/non-GAAP operating-margin or gross-margin PERCENTAGE for the reported quarter - only dollar figures (op income $2.24B GAAP / $2.95B non-GAAP on $6.618B revenue). The only 'operating margin %' text anywhere in the release belongs to the Q3 and FY26 guidance sections (44.0% / 45.0% non-GAAP), so a naive extractor grabbing the first operating-margin percentage risks reporting next quarter's target as this quarter's actual. GAAP diluted EPS ($4.25) includes a $0.17/share one-time goodwill impairment on the Publishing & Advertising unit.

ACN.notes: Accenture's only non-GAAP ('adjusted') EPS/operating-margin reconciliation in this release covers the nine-month YTD column, not the quarter - Q3 alone had $0 business-optimization costs on the income statement, so quarterly GAAP and adjusted EPS are identical ($3.80), but a parser could easily grab the 9-month adjusted EPS ($10.67) thinking it is the quarter. op_margin is null despite a prominent '17.0%' GAAP operating-margin bullet because no non-GAAP-labeled quarterly operating margin is ever stated (adjusted operating margin is given only for the 9-month YTD, 15.9%, and as FY26 guidance, 15.8%). The outlook table shows both the new (June 18) and prior (March 19) full-year guidance side by side: EPS guidance's low end was raised ($13.25->$13.38 GAAP) but revenue-growth guidance's high end was cut (5%->4% local currency) - a genuinely mixed revision with no 'raise'/'lower' language anywhere, hence null.

COST.notes: Costco's income statement gives both a quarter (12-week) and YTD (36-week) column, but the headline 11.6% growth figure refers to 'Net sales' ($69.15B) while a separate 'Total revenue' line ($70.53B) adds membership fees - the true top-line total used here. The cash-flow statement, unlike the income statement, is presented ONLY for the 36-week YTD period, so the $4,228M capex figure is nine-months cumulative, not the quarter, and no standalone-quarter capex appears anywhere. Costco gives no forward guidance of any kind and reports no non-GAAP figures or gross/operating margin percentages in this release, so those fields are genuinely null, not omissions.

NKE.notes: Gross margin of 49.2% (+890 bps YoY) is overwhelmingly a one-time effect - Nike states a ~900 bps benefit from an expected IEEPA tariff-recovery windfall, so underlying gross margin was roughly flat YoY; GAAP EPS of $0.72 similarly includes a stated $0.52/share benefit from the same one-time item, and Nike never publishes an ex-item 'adjusted EPS' to net it out. The income statement has no 'Operating income' line at all - Nike uses 'EBIT margin' (12.0% for Q4, explicitly labeled non-GAAP) instead - and this release contains no cash-flow statement (so no capex figure) and no forward guidance of any kind.

FDX.notes: CRITICAL: this filing is NOT an earnings release. FedEx changed its fiscal year end (May 31 -> Dec 31) and spun off FedEx Freight effective June 1, 2026; the most-recent-by-date Item 2.02 8-K (filed 2026-07-21, accession 0001048911-26-000108) is purely 'Supplemental Historical Financial Information' recasting CY2024/CY2025 quarters onto the new calendar-quarter/segment structure - it has no revenue, EPS, or guidance for any period not already reported. It DOES contain quarter-labeled EPS tables (e.g. 'FOURTH QUARTER CALENDAR 2025 ... GAAP $5.85, Non-GAAP $5.88') that a naive extractor could easily mistake for a fresh quarterly result. FedEx's actual last real earnings release (Q4 FY2026, quarter ended May 31, 2026) is a DIFFERENT, earlier 8-K filed 2026-06-23, accession 0001048911-26-000050 - which recent_8k()'s 'newest Item 2.02' logic skips right past. All fields are null here by necessity, not because the release omitted them.

LEN.notes: Total consolidated revenue actually fell ~5.2% YoY ($7.94B vs $8.38B, computed) even though the only stated growth figure in the release is 'Revenues from home sales decreased 2%' - a narrower Homebuilding sub-line that excludes much sharper declines in Multifamily and Financial Services revenue; a parser keying off the headline '-2%' would be wrong for total revenue. 'Gross margin' (15.6%) is specifically 'gross margin on home sales' (Homebuilding-only), not a consolidated figure, and there is no cash-flow statement or capex figure anywhere in the release. Next-quarter guidance is given only as units x price (deliveries 20,500-21,500 at $375-380K ASP), not a revenue dollar range, while full-year DELIVERY guidance was explicitly 'moderat[ed] ... to approximately 82,000 to 83,000 homes' - a plain lowering, though of unit deliveries, not revenue or EPS (Lennar gives no full-year $ guidance at all).

GIS.notes: GAAP diluted EPS was a LOSS of $(3.74) this quarter (driven by a $1.8B non-cash goodwill/brand impairment plus a $1.0B Brazil-divestiture valuation loss, both booked in 'Restructuring, transformation, impairment, and other exit costs' of $2,808M), while adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was a positive $0.95 - an enormous GAAP/non-GAAP gap that a naive extractor grabbing 'diluted EPS' without checking for the loss/adjusted split would badly misreport. The cash-flow statement (and its capex line, $539.9M) is disclosed only for the full fiscal year, never the quarter, and forward guidance covers only fiscal 2027 in full-year growth-rate terms (no quarter, no dollar figures) - and since this is the first time FY2027 targets are issued, guide_raised is null rather than a guess.

KMX.notes: CarMax never uses the words 'gross margin' or 'operating margin' anywhere in the release - there is no 'Operating income' subtotal at all in the income statement (it goes straight from Gross Profit + CAF income, minus SG&A/D&A/interest, to pretax earnings), so op_margin has nothing to extract; the 10.7% gross-margin figure used here is inferred from the 'Gross Profit' percent-of-revenue column in the Selected Operating Ratios table. CarMax gives zero forward guidance of any kind (no revenue, EPS, or margin targets) - the only forward-looking numeric is a standing $200M SG&A cost-reduction target for the end of FY2027, which is not a guidance range.

PAYX.notes: The cash-flow statement (and its $234.9M capex line) is presented only for the full twelve months, never the quarter, matching a pattern seen elsewhere in this batch (ORCL, GIS, COST) - no standalone Q4 capex is disclosed. FY2027 guidance is a growth-rate-only range (revenue +5% to +6%) for the FULL YEAR, with no quarter-specific or dollar figures, and the phrase 'updated business outlook' hints this may revise an earlier preliminary FY2027 outlook without showing the prior numbers or using 'raise'/'lower' language, so guide_raised is null rather than guessed. Paychex never uses the term 'gross margin' anywhere in the release (only a bare 'Cost of service revenue' expense line), so that field has nothing to extract.

CCL.notes: 'Gross margin' means something different for Carnival than for most companies: it is reported only as a dollar figure and as a $-per-ALBD 'yield' (e.g. 'Gross margin yields down 3.9 percent' is a YoY change in that per-ALBD yield, not a margin-of-revenue ratio) - Carnival never states a gross-margin percentage of revenue anywhere, so a parser matching 'gross margin' plus a percent sign would badly misread that headline bullet as the margin level itself. Total revenue's YoY growth is never stated directly (only EPS +15%, net income +20%+, and net yields +2.2% are called out) - it must be computed from the income statement ($6,663M vs $6,328M = +5.3%). Q3/full-year guidance is entirely in yield/growth-rate terms (no dollar revenue), and while the release notes Q2 actual results 'exceed[ed] our March guidance by $100 million,' there is no explicit 'raise'/'lower' language for the forward full-year outlook.

DAL.notes: Delta reports two entirely different 'total revenue' figures for the same quarter: GAAP $19,757M (includes ~$2.1B of third-party fuel-refinery sales) vs. non-GAAP $17,666M (excludes it) - and Delta's own prose calls the SMALLER, adjusted figure 'total revenue' ('total revenue increased 14 percent ... to a record $17.7 billion'), while GAAP growth for the same quarter is 19%. Full-year guidance is explicitly 'Affirm[ed]' (maintained, not raised/lowered), and next-quarter (September) revenue guidance is only a qualitative rate ('up mid-teens'), never a dollar range. The line Delta itself labels 'Gross capital expenditures' ($1,442M) is already a lightly non-GAAP-adjusted figure - true unadjusted GAAP capex is Flight equipment $1,244M + Ground property $214M = $1,458M.

AZO.notes: Diluted EPS of $38.07 is genuinely correct, not a data error - AutoZone has never split its stock (shares trade near $3,500+), so any EPS sanity-range check would wrongly flag it. Gross margin (52.2%, GAAP; AutoZone has no non-GAAP EPS or margin at all) fell YoY specifically due to 'a 77 basis point net non-cash LIFO impact.' There is no precise operating-margin percentage in the structured tables, only a CEO quote citing margin 'north of 19%' (computed GAAP figure is 19.1%), and no revenue/EPS guidance anywhere - AutoZone's only forward-looking number is a store-count target (355-365 new stores for the full fiscal year).

AVGO.notes: Broadcom's income statement labels a DOLLAR subtotal 'Gross margin' ($20,456M GAAP / $22,191M non-GAAP) - no percentage is stated anywhere in the release (computed: 69.1% GAAP / 75.0% non-GAAP), so an extractor could easily report the dollar figure as if it were a rate. The only operating-margin PERCENTAGE anywhere (66%, 'flat from a year ago') is Q4 GUIDANCE, not Q3 actual, and it sits suspiciously close to the true computed Q3 non-GAAP operating margin (67.9% = $20,095M/$29,591M), making a guidance/actual mix-up hard to catch. Broadcom gives only single-point next-quarter guidance ($34.8B revenue, no range) and no full-year outlook at all in this release, so guide_raised has nothing to compare against.

CIEN.notes: This filing is comparatively clean: gross margin (46.4% non-GAAP) and operating margin (22.5% non-GAAP) are both explicitly stated as percentages in a summary table, and guidance explicitly separates a point-plus-range next-quarter figure (Q4: $1.75B +/- $50M) from full-year guidance that is explicitly 'Raising ... to $6.42 billion' - an unambiguous raised case. The one real trap: the cash-flow statement covers only the nine months ended, so there is no standalone Q3 capex figure anywhere in the release (the $194.9M 'Payments for equipment' line is 9-month cumulative, not the quarter).

JBL.notes: No operating-margin percentage is ever stated for the ACTUAL Q3 results (only dollar figures: GAAP $445M / core $504M operating income on $8,751M revenue) - the only operating-margin percent anywhere in the release (5.8% non-GAAP) is FULL-YEAR FY2026 GUIDANCE, and it sits almost exactly at the computed actual Q3 core margin (5.76%), so a guidance/actual swap would be nearly invisible. Revenue growth (11.8%) and gross margin are likewise never stated as percentages anywhere, only dollars, and the cash-flow statement covers nine months only (no standalone Q3 capex). Jabil explicitly calls these 'preliminary, unaudited' results subject to revision when finalized.

RH.notes: RH's 'adjusted' (non-GAAP) figures are WORSE than GAAP this quarter - the reverse of the usual pattern - because GAAP results include a $31.7M one-time LEGAL SETTLEMENT GAIN that adjusted figures strip out: GAAP diluted EPS is $(0.73) but adjusted diluted EPS is $(1.97), and GAAP operating margin is 4.3% vs adjusted operating margin of just 0.3%. Full-year and Q2 guidance are both growth-RATE ranges only (FY: revenue +4.5% to +8.0%; Q2: +0.5% to +2.5%), never dollar figures, though the release does explicitly say 'we are raising our outlook for fiscal year 2026.' The filing is RH's usual long-form shareholder-letter narrative rather than a conventional numbers-first release, which could confuse section-based extraction heuristics.

SIG.notes: GAAP diluted EPS ($0.78) coincidentally equals the disclosed per-share restructuring/other-charges impact ('$0.78 of restructuring and other charges net of taxes') - two different concepts sharing the same number; adjusted diluted EPS ($1.56) is exactly GAAP EPS plus that add-back. Guidance is unusually clean here: the release shows 'Updated' vs. 'Previous' FY2027 figures side by side, and every metric's low end (both ends for EPS: $8.80-$10.74 to $9.20-$11.00) moved up, matching the explicit headline 'Raising FY27 Adjusted EPS Guidance.' The prior-year same-store-sales comp (2.7%) has itself been restated under a new methodology, so it doesn't match what Signet originally reported a year ago for that quarter.

PLAY.notes: No capex line item appears anywhere in this release - the Summary Cash Flow table shows only NET investing activities (mixing capex with sale-leaseback proceeds), and even the Adjusted Free Cash Flow reconciliation shows just the final $25.3M result without its 'less Capital Expenditures' component broken out. Dave & Buster's has no 'gross margin' concept at all (cost of entertainment/food-and-beverage are each expressed as % of their OWN revenue line, not total revenue); a likely trap is 'Store Operating Income Before D&A' (27.3% of revenue), a materially narrower non-GAAP metric excluding G&A and pre-opening costs, easily mistaken for an 'adjusted operating margin' this release never actually provides. There is no revenue, EPS, or margin guidance anywhere for next quarter or the full year - only a vague aspiration to generate 'over $100 million' in FY2026 free cash flow.

CHWY.notes: Chewy prominently states 'Adjusted EBITDA margin' (7.5%) but never states an operating-margin percentage (GAAP or non-GAAP) anywhere - EBITDA margin adds back depreciation & amortization on top of the usual stock-comp/severance/transaction addbacks, so it is not interchangeable with 'adjusted operating margin' (computable but unstated: $128.5M op income / $3,357.2M net sales = 3.8% GAAP). There is no revenue, EPS, or margin guidance anywhere in the release for next quarter or the full year. Quarterly capex ($37.7M) is disclosed cleanly and, by coincidence, is numerically identical to the prior-year quarter's capex.

ZS.notes: Zscaler defines 'capex' as the SUM of 'Purchases of property, equipment and other assets' ($199.8M) PLUS 'Capitalized internal-use software' ($18.7M) = $218.5M (their own prose states this combined figure) - grabbing only the PP&E line would understate capex by about 9%. The 25% reported revenue growth is inflated by the Red Canary acquisition (ex-acquisition ARR growth was only 20% for the quarter; an ex-acquisition revenue growth figure, 20%, is given only for the full year, not Q4 alone), and the GAAP net loss ($3.4M) versus non-GAAP net income ($198.2M) gap is driven mostly by $215.2M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes. Q4 actual non-GAAP operating margin (24%, called 'a record') sits right next to Q1 FY2027 GUIDANCE of 23% - close but different periods, an easy mix-up. This is also the first FY2027 guide issued, so guide_raised is null rather than a guess.

AVAV.notes: Hand-read 2026-09-10 from the 8-K accepted 2026-09-09 16:04:03 ET. Added because no filing in the original key had AeroVironment's two traps. (1) The income statement's TOTAL revenue line carries no row label - 'Revenue:' captions the components (Product sales 329,058 / Contract services 151,432) and the total 480,490 sits unlabelled beneath them, so every name-based rule returns a component. (2) The 'Reportable Segment Results' table is headed AxS | SCDE | Total, putting the column word 'Total' directly in front of the row label 'Revenue'; the fused 'Total Revenue' outranked the income statement and put one segment ($345,969) on the panel as the quarter with a second segment ($134,521) as the year-ago column - reported as +157% growth and, against a $468M consensus, as a 26% revenue MISS when the quarter was a $480.5M BEAT. gross_margin is the stated 26% (124,599/480,490 = 25.9%); the quarter is an operating LOSS so op_margin is left null. guide_raised is null: 'continues to expect' reaffirms FY27, it neither raises nor lowers.
